question:
Optex Systems Holdings (NASDAQ: OPXS) is headquartered in Richardson, Texas. Per its FY2025 10-K it designs and makes optical sighting systems and assemblies for defense customers (periscopes for vehicles such as Abrams, Bradley and Stryker; rifle and surveillance sights; night vision optical assemblies), plus optical coatings at its Applied Optics Center in Dallas. FY2025 revenue was about $41.3M across two segments (Richardson $23.8M, Applied Optics Center $17.6M external). The Richardson site is about 49,100 sq ft with 87 FTEs on a single shift. Products are mostly build-to-print. Contracts often require first article acceptance and testing.

Workflow to assess (chosen by the author, not by Optex): nonconformance triage and material review board (MRB) preparation. The 10-K lists, among cost-control practices, an ISO 9001:2008 certificate with annual surveillance audits, weekly cycle counts, and a weekly material review board meeting on non-moving piece parts, and says the company is implementing the shop floor control module of its ERP. It also notes single-source suppliers for some contracts. An assumed pain point that follows: each week a quality engineer gathers open nonconformances, inspection results, supplier history and part status from several places to build the MRB packet.

Systems: the ERP is referenced in the 10-K, but its vendor is not confirmed in public filings, so it is assumed. Nonconformance and inspection record formats are assumed.

Pilot idea: a narrow multi-agent assistant that pulls open nonconformances and related inspection notes, groups them by part, supplier and defect type, attaches relevant history, drafts a suggested disposition category with a short justification, and assembles the weekly MRB packet. A quality engineer approves every disposition. Nothing is scrapped, reworked or returned automatically.

Constraints (assumed): technical data is ITAR-controlled, so any model and all data must stay in an approved environment; no public model endpoints. 90 days, Richardson site, small quality team. Success means faster MRB prep and lower nonconformance age. All checklist answers are outside-in assumptions.
